Игра NARAKA: BLADEPOINT – это глоток свежего воздуха в жанре королевской битвы. Уникальная механика боя, основанная на парировании, уклонении и выстраивании стамин-менеджмента, делает каждую схватку напряженной и захватывающей. Система захвата крюком позволяет молниеносно перемещаться по карте и устраивать засады, добавляя вертикальности в геймплей.

Визуальный стиль игры, вдохновленный азиатской мифологией, впечатляет детализированными локациями и проработанными моделями персонажей. Разнообразие героев с уникальными способностями и стилями боя радует, позволяя каждому найти своего фаворита.

Однако, новичкам игра может показаться сложной из-за высокого порога вхождения в боевую систему. Требуется время, чтобы освоить механики парирования и контр-атак. Также, игра требует мощного железа для комфортной игры на высоких настройках.

Несмотря на это, NARAKA: BLADEPOINT предлагает захватывающий и уникальный опыт для любителей королевских битв и файтингов, способный затянуть на долгие часы. Игра постоянно обновляется, добавляя новый контент и улучшая баланс, что делает её всё более привлекательной.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that inventory management and looting during matches feel clunky and chaotic.

citations.review_text:
NetEase's Latest Free-to-Play Brawler: A Solid Contender with Some Strings Attached

NetEase has a knack for delivering polished free games, and this one is no exception—think Fortnite's fast-paced chaos stripped of the toxic lobbies, flashy cosmetics, and griefers. The core gameplay is a blast: snappy, melee-focused action with grapple hooks enabling deadly combo attacks that feel borderline overpowered. Ranged options exist but wisely take a backseat, keeping the emphasis on close-quarters frenzy. Matches are simple yet addictive, perfect for quick sessions.

Visually, it's stunning—vibrant arenas that run buttery smooth once you tweak the settings. I shaved off a noticeable input lag (a few milliseconds on defaults) via the options menu, transforming it from "good" to "better."

That said, inventory management is a pain, especially in full servers. Picking up loot or swapping gear mid-fight? Good luck—it's clunky and chaotic, possibly by design to amp up the tension. NetEase's signature menu overload is here too, burying you in layers of options and purchases(either real or game loot).

A quick note on game hiccups: HCVI (anti-cheat) was disabled initially, sparking some community panic, but the November 2025 update fixed it. Data privacy concerns linger—NetEase loves collecting user info—but I found no reports of intentional hacking or intrusion into a user's PC.  However tons of accounts getting hacked via phishing not on NetEase's fault list though.

Broader gripes: NetEase's aggressive acquisitions of indie studios and franchises, followed by shutdowns or content locks, sour the experience. It's predatory and kills promising projects players were hyped for.

FINAL Verdict: 8.9/10
Deducting a full point for the menu maze (classic NetEase) and 0.1 for the publisher drama. If you can overlook the corporate baggage, this is a must-try freebie.

citations.review_text:
It was weird when it released, but it has gotten much better over  years. I’ve been playing on and off for years and finally decided to write a review.

On the plus side: The gameplay loop is fun, there is a plenty of different modes, and you don't even need to play against real players if you don't want to. (Expert bots are better than 70% of the playerbase, beware, they are scary). The game also has good optimization.

On the downside: Most players are on the asian server, so expect longer queue times if you are elsewhere. The learning curve is also rather steep; being stunlocked until you figure out all the animation cancels and timings is basically a given. (Again, expert bots are a good learning tool here).

Overall, if you are interested in wuxia themes, battle royale, or extraction modes, it's definitely worth a try. Game is f2p but you can only buy cosmetics, no gameplay related power items.

NARAKA: BLADEPOINT is one of the most unique battle royale games I've played.

The melee-focused combat is what makes it stand out. Instead of just shooting from a distance, fights are fast, intense, and require good timing, movement, and mind games. Winning a duel feels incredibly satisfying.

The movement system is also a huge part of the fun. Grappling around the map, chasing enemies, escaping bad situations, and pulling off plays that look straight out of an action movie never gets old.

The learning curve can be rough at first, and you'll probably get destroyed by experienced players while learning the combat. But once everything starts clicking, the game becomes very rewarding.

The visuals, character designs, and overall style are also great and help the game stand out from other battle royales.

Not the easiest game to get into, but definitely one of the most unique and satisfying once you do.

I’ve played a lot of battle royale games over the years, but honestly, Naraka: Bladepoint feels like something completely different in the best possible way. Most BR games focus only on guns and positioning, but Naraka mixes fast-paced movement, intense melee combat, grappling hooks, mind games, and mechanical skill in a way that feels incredibly satisfying once you get into it.

At first, the game can feel overwhelming. There are so many mechanics to learn — combos, counters, focus attacks, movement tech, hero abilities, weapon matchups, and timing. But that’s exactly why the game feels rewarding. Every fight feels like an actual duel instead of just “who saw who first.” When you win a fight in Naraka, it genuinely feels earned.

One of my favorite things about the game is the movement system. The grappling hook alone makes traversal insanely fun. Flying through trees, chasing enemies across rooftops, escaping impossible situations, or suddenly turning a fight around with mobility never gets old. The game feels fast, fluid, and stylish almost all the time.

The combat is probably the strongest part of the game. It’s easy to understand the basics, but there’s a very high skill ceiling. Good players can outplay opponents through timing, reads, positioning, and smart decision-making instead of pure luck. Every weapon also has its own personality. Some weapons feel aggressive and explosive, while others reward patience and precision. Learning different weapons keeps the gameplay fresh even after many hours.

Visually, the game is beautiful. The environments, character designs, outfits, animations, and overall atmosphere are genuinely impressive. The art direction gives the game a unique identity compared to other battle royale titles. Some moments honestly feel like scenes from a martial arts movie.

In terms of pure gameplay, Naraka is a great and unique battle royale. The combat feels great, the characters and their abilities are well designed and fun to use. It essentially is fighting game style combat with a mix of moba / hero shooter esque character abilties and ultimates. It also offers an insane level of character customization where you can really go off on the details if you enjoy that.

However, the reality of the gameplay experience has a few glaring issues, mostly related to the game's lack of popularity in the west. Essentially 95% + of the playerbase is Chinese, playing on the CN server. The other servers have an extremely small population. It is extremely easy to become a top 500 player or a top 100 on the leaderboard of a certain character because the amount of people playing on the NA / EU servers is so small. ( That's why its funny that some of the people in these reviews are saying proudly that they're top 500, lol sweetie we all are.)

This lack of playerbase leads to the biggest issue of playing on NA servers: the queue times. In the earlier ranks, queues will be manageable because the lobbies are completely full of bots, but when you get to higher ranks they become ridiculous. Outside of peak gameplay times, I struggle to get games at all and regularly wait 15-30 min and straight up have my queue time out. 

During more popular times its still a dice roll whether the queue will pop within 10-15 min. When I do get into a game, its with the same 10 people who I see over and over, the top ranked people on the server because those are the only people who play the game in NA. This obviously gets tiring quickly. It's a shame because if the game had a healthy population in the west it would be a blast.

Its possible to play on the Chinese server with some workaround but if you are in the US the ping will be very high. However, the queue times are only 1-2 min at all times and the lobby is full of actual players. It creates a sad dilemma for NA/EU …

citations.review_text:
It was weird when it released, but it has gotten much better over  years. I’ve been playing on and off for years and finally decided to write a review.

On the plus side: The gameplay loop is fun, there is a plenty of different modes, and you don't even need to play against real players if you don't want to. (Expert bots are better than 70% of the playerbase, beware, they are scary). The game also has good optimization.

On the downside: Most players are on the asian server, so expect longer queue times if you are elsewhere. The learning curve is also rather steep; being stunlocked until you figure out all the animation cancels and timings is basically a given. (Again, expert bots are a good learning tool here).

Overall, if you are interested in wuxia themes, battle royale, or extraction modes, it's definitely worth a try. Game is f2p but you can only buy cosmetics, no gameplay related power items.

After 1,000 hours in NARAKA: BLADEPOINT, I can say the game offers a great variety of modes, whether you prefer PvE, PvPvE, or classic PvP. Overall, the gameplay is excellent, but the UI is one of the game’s weakest aspects. It feels overly cluttered, almost like a pilot’s cockpit, and navigating through menus can be frustrating at first. However, once you get used to it, it becomes manageable.

The combat system is the game’s biggest strength. The fighting-game-style mechanics, including combos, blocking, and parrying, are both fun and complex, allowing for a high skill ceiling and many different playstyles. It genuinely feels like a unique and well-designed fighting battle royale experience.

That said, the game’s performance and server issues have become increasingly frustrating. The amount of high-ping players, especially players joining from other regions just to gank newer players, can make matches feel unfair. On top of that, the optimization has noticeably worsened over time. I used to run the game smoothly on my low-end laptop, but now I experience constant lag spikes, with my ping jumping from 60 to 200 unexpectedly, making the game almost unplayable at times.

Recently, the game feels like it has been going downhill due to these technical issues. If the developers do not improve the optimization and server stability soon, I may stop playing until those problems are properly addressed.

The combat system is the game’s biggest strength. The fighting-game-style mechanics, including combos, blocking, and parrying, are both fun and complex, allowing for a high skill ceiling and many different playstyles. It genuinely feels like a unique and well-designed fighting battle royale experience.

That said, the game’s performance and server issues have become increasingly frustrating. The amount of high-ping players, especially players joining from other regions just to gank newer players, can make matches feel unfair. On top of that, the optimization has noticeably worsened over time. I used to run the game smoothly on my low-end laptop, but now I experience constant lag spikes, with my ping jumping from 60 to 200 unexpectedly, making the game almost unplayable at times.

Recently, the game feels like it has been going downhill due to these technical issues. If the developers do not improve the optimization and server stability soon, I may stop playing until those problems are properly addressed.

Naraka is a Chinese game that had the potential to be a fairly decent FG-based multiplayer product but made the incredibly unfortunate decision to use Unity and is built by a team whose only experience with Unity is transactional netcode in cellphone games. Given that Unity is a poorly-performing disaster of a cash grab at the best of times one can only expect good things when the greed of both worlds unite in a singular hyper-sticky smile-inducing idol-glazing handshake.

Naraka is plagued by technical issues of the most absurd nature. Just like Fallout 76 it uses no Delta Timers, so animation speeds and thus their notifies (damage events, for example) are completely dictated by FPS. This means everything from combos to float times to locomotion are entirely dictated by your processor and being on the receiving end of a hardware diff is a lot like being abducted by ET and having your genitals sucked clean off by little green men. CN tournaments have an FPS cap, but everywhere else in the game world is a wild west where the game's extremely CPU cache hungry performance problems render it virtually unplayable for anyone not using an X3d processor. If you're sub 300 FPS many core mechanics of the game will become so inconsistent you'll be convinced many of the double-digit players that still actively play this product in NA are hacking, when in reality they're just paying over a thousand dollarydoos for the exclusive opportunity of having an advantage in a dead game. That isn't to say the game isn't filled with hackers, though - only CN has an active moderation team, and Doujin is still filled with endless videos of people blatantly changing memory values willy nilly to fly around, machinegun slap people to death in Penglai, grab and teleport people into the skybox and other goofy nonsense.
